headline: High-risk default interaction: Langflow can ingest and act on ComfyUI outputs, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP, but Langflow can chain multiple agents and wire tools into flow nodes, so ComfyUI outputs can become Langflow inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if generated content is treated as text. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text is passed into a Langflow prompt or parser
IF Langflow flow nodes treat upstream content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every ComfyUI output before passing it onward
Insert a manual review step before any Langflow prompt node
Disable any flow node that parses raw model output as instructions
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, models, and files, while Langflow reads and writes server files and can send data to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services. If the pair shares a workspace or uploaded files, sensitive media or model artifacts can flow from A into B and then out to third parties. The default egress on B makes the blast radius broader than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or uploaded file store
IF Langflow components forward ComfyUI artifacts to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Separate the two agents onto different workspaces
Restrict Langflow components to approved endpoints only
Remove sensitive media from any shared upload folder
Turn off automatic file forwarding in flows
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and audit logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI does not write the filesystem, but Langflow does, reads files, and runs unsandboxed Python by default. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, Langflow can overwrite or consume ComfyUI assets and server-side state without coordination. Because B has broad write and subprocess capability, the default conflict risk is high even though A is mostly read-only.
conditions: IF Langflow and ComfyUI share a writable directory
IF Langflow Python components modify files that ComfyUI also loads
mitigations: Use separate directories for models and flow state
Run Langflow with a read-only mount to ComfyUI assets
Disable unsandboxed Python components for shared paths
Pause one agent before bulk file writes in the other
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow system that can chain multiple agents and wire tools into nodes, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative unless the flow author adds checks. ComfyUI produces generated content and workflows that Langflow may consume as inputs. That makes a default cascade from A’s output into B’s actions plausible, with high blast radius if B triggers external services.
conditions: IF a Langflow flow uses ComfyUI output as a downstream prompt or decision input
IF downstream Langflow nodes call external APIs based on that output
mitigations: Add a verification node between ComfyUI and any action-taking step
Require human approval before external API calls
Log and inspect intermediate outputs for hallucinated facts
Limit flows to read-only transformations
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on upstream outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented in either profile. ComfyUI is offline and local by default, while Langflow can send flow data to external providers, so compliance risk appears only if regulated data is routed through those external calls. Because the pair itself does not prove a breach, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into a Langflow flow that calls external providers
IF deployment policy requires local-only processing but Langflow endpoints remain enabled
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Langflow flows
Disable external provider components for sensitive projects
Review retention settings for stored flow secrets
Use local-only model endpoints where possible
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
